newsitem.title: CUBA: Cuba opens first free trade zone.
newsitem.headline: Cuba opens first free trade zone.

text.p: Cuba opened the first of four planned free trade zones on Monday, as part of a strategy to attract more foreign investment to the island.

The Wajay Free Trade Zone, sited at an existing warehouse complex near Havana international airport, was inaugurated in a brief ceremony by Cuban Foreign Investment Minister Ibrahim Ferradaz and Foreign Trade Minister Ricardo Cabrisas.
It will be run by a Cuban corporation, Almacenes Universales S.A., which is linked to Cuba's Revolutionary Armed Forces (FAR).

Almacenes Universales Vice-President Roberto Perez told reporters that nearly 30 foreign companies would initially operate at the zone. Of these, more than 20 had already been using warehouse consignment facilities offered at the Wajay site over the last three years.
New operators in the free trade zone consisted of four manufacturers and one services company. Three of these firms were from Spain and the others from Italy and Jamaica.

The Jamaican company, Eurolatina Corp, which is backed by British capital, was set to become the first foreign manufacturer to set up in a Cuban free trade zone. Its factory at Wajay to produce powdered flavored drinks was due to be completed at the end of this month.

Cuba plans to set up three more free trade zones and industrial parks, where foreign companies are being offered tax breaks and other operating concessions to produce goods and services principally for export.

One of these, at Berroa, just east of Havana, is also expected to be inaugurated this week. The others, at the ports of Mariel, west of Havana, and Cienfuegos, in south central Cuba, are expected to be opened over the course of this year.

Cuba, squeezed by the U.S. Helms-Burton law that tightens Washington's 35-year-old economic embargo against the island, is trying to attract more foreign investment to maximize its hard currency exports, revitalize recession-hit industries and generate new jobs.
In a separate ceremony Monday, a British company signed a contract to provide airport management consultancy services to Cuba's biggest airports, at Havana and the resort of Varadero.

Under the three-year contract, Leeds-based Airport Planning and Development Ltd agreed to help Cuba's Empresa Cubana de Aeropuertos y Servicios Aeroportuarios (ECASA) to run the two airports at international standards.
Airport Planning would work in partnership with another British company, Airport Commercial Ventures.
Cuba's Havana and Varadero airports are both being modernized and expanded to cope with growing tourist traffic.
